questions.stem: This question is about alkenes and alkanes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table by giving the missing information about the alkene with the molecular formula $ \mathrm{C_{3}H_{6}} $

parts.label: b
parts.text: Alkenes are unsaturated compounds.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State what is meant by the term unsaturated.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Describe a test to show that a compound is unsaturated.

parts.label: c
parts.text: When the alkane methane reacts with chlorine, the products are chloromethane $ \mathrm{(C H_{3} C l)} $ and hydrogen chloride gas.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Give a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: What is the name of this type of reaction? A addition B decomposition neutralisation substitution

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: State the condition needed for this reaction to occur.

parts.label: d
parts.text: When ethane reacts with chlorine, one of the products of the reaction has the formula $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{4} Cl_{2}} $ There are two isomers with this formula.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: State what is meant by the term isomers.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Draw the displayed formulae of the two isomers with the formula $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{4} Cl_{2}} $

questions.stem: A solution of hydrogen peroxide decomposes when a catalyst of manganese(IV) oxide is added. The products of the reaction are water and oxygen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give a test for oxygen.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the reason for adding a catalyst.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A student investigates how changing the concentration of the hydrogen peroxide solution affects the rate of this reaction. She uses this apparatus. The student records the volume of oxygen that collects every 2 minutes for 16 minutes. The table shows her results.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Plot the student's results on the grid.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Draw a circle on the grid around the anomalous result.

parts.label: d-iii
parts.text: Draw a curve of best fit through the points, ignoring the anomalous result.

parts.label: d-iv
parts.text: Suggest a mistake that the student might have made to cause the anomalous result.

parts.label: d-v
parts.text: Determine the volume of oxygen collected during the first 3 minutes. Show on your graph how you obtain your answer.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The student repeats the experiment using hydrogen peroxide solution of half the concentration of the original solution. She keeps the volume of the hydrogen peroxide solution and all other conditions the same.

parts.label: e-i
parts.text: Draw on the grid the curve you would expect the student to obtain.

parts.label: e-ii
parts.text: Explain how using hydrogen peroxide solution of half the concentration affects the rate of the reaction. Refer to particle collision theory in your answer.

questions.stem: A student uses the reaction between zinc and dilute sulfuric acid to prepare some zinc sulfate crystals.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the equation for this reaction by giving the correct state symbols. $\mathrm {Z n} (\dots \dots \dots \dots) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} (\dots \dots \dots \dots) \rightarrow \mathrm {Z n S O} _ {4} (\dots \dots \dots \dots) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} (\dots \dots \dots \dots)$

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State what would be observed during this reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The student adds excess zinc to a beaker of dilute sulfuric acid.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Explain why it is necessary to add excess zinc.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Draw a diagram of the apparatus the student should use to remove the unreacted zinc and collect the zinc sulfate solution.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student obtains a pure, dry sample of zinc sulfate crystals. The formula of zinc sulfate crystals is $ \mathrm{Z n S O_{4}. 7 H_{2} O} $

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass $ ( M_{r} ) $ of zinc sulfate crystals. $M _ {\mathrm {r}} =$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: The student uses 0.0200 mol of dilute sulfuric acid in her preparation. Show that the maximum mass of zinc sulfate crystals that the student could obtain is about 6 g.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: The student obtains a mass of 4.28 g of zinc sulfate crystals. Calculate the percentage yield of the zinc sulfate crystals. Give your answer to three significant figures.

questions.stem: (a) A piece of magnesium ribbon is ignited and placed in a gas jar of oxygen. The equation for the reaction is $2 \mathrm {M g} + \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {M g O}$ (i) Give two observations that would be made in this reaction. (ii) State why this is an oxidation reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A second piece of magnesium ribbon is ignited and placed in a gas jar of carbon dioxide. A very exothermic reaction occurs, forming magnesium oxide and carbon.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State what is meant by the term exothermic.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Give the chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: A fire starts in a warehouse where magnesium is stored. Suggest why it would not be suitable to use a carbon dioxide fire extinguisher to put out this fire.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A student uses this apparatus to find the mass of magnesium oxide that forms when a known mass of magnesium is heated. This is his method. find the mass of the crucible and lid place some magnesium ribbon in the crucible heat the crucible with the lid on for a few minutes find the mass of the crucible, lid and magnesium find the mass of the crucible, lid and magnesium oxide Using this method, the mass of magnesium oxide formed is less than expected. Explain two changes that the student should make to his method to obtain a mass of magnesium oxide closer to the expected mass.
